headline: Hackers influence ChatGPT and Gemini to redirect users to scam sites
summary: Cybercriminals are exploiting vulnerabilities in popular AI chatbots to trick users into visiting malicious websites.
details: New reports indicate that hackers have found ways to manipulate large language models like OpenAI's ChatGPT and Google's Gemini.
These malicious actors are able to influence the AI's responses, subtly guiding users towards phishing and scam websites.
The exact methods used to exploit these models are still under investigation, but the implications for user safety are significant.
This vulnerability highlights the evolving landscape of cyber threats as AI becomes more integrated into daily online activities.
caption:
AI chatbots like ChatGPT and Gemini are being hijacked by hackers to send users to scam sites.

New reports indicate that hackers have found ways to manipulate large language models like OpenAI's ChatGPT and Google's Gemini.

These malicious actors are able to influence the AI's responses, subtly guiding users towards phishing and scam websites.

The exact methods used to exploit these models are still under investigation, but the implications for user safety are significant.

This vulnerability highlights the evolving landscape of cyber threats as AI becomes more integrated into daily online activities.

Source: Hacker News
